message.reasoning_content:
Looking at this, the target interface is cpu_smt_mask with the consumer phase being CPUHP_AP_SCHED_STARTING via sched_cpu_starting. I note that cpu_smt_mask is only defined as a generic fallback when CONFIG_SCHED_SMT is set and no architecture-specific macro already overrides it.

The actual consumers are sched_core_cpu_starting() and sched_core_lock(), which call cpu_smt_mask(cpu) to determine SMT sibling groupings for core scheduling and to establish a consistent CPU locking order during hotplug startup. This means the contract requires cpu_smt_mask(cpu) to correctly reflect which CPUs share a physical core, with the mask properly initialized before sched_cpu_starting runs - and since architectures can override the macro, different platforms (like s390 with book/drawer topology) may implement this differently.

The real concern is ordering: does topology data get populated (via arch_update_cpu_topology or set_cpu_sibling_map, typically in start_secondary before notify_cpu_starting) before sched_core_cpu_starting consumes it at CPUHP_AP_SCHED_STARTING? The notify_cpu_starting documentation only guarantees it runs before interrupts are enabled, not that topology masks are already set, so this is worth checking as a genuine initialization-order dependency.

I'm drafting this as a finding titled around cpu_smt_mask depending on arch code having already populated sibling masks before sched_cpu_starting consumes them, with the contract being that when CONFIG_SCHED_SMT is on and no arch override exists, cpu_smt_mask falls back to topology_sibling_cpumask(cpu).

The architecture_difference section notes the material only gives the generic fallback definition, with no arch-specific override or sibling mask timing source shown, so the actual cross-arch variation is unknown. The propagation chain flows from topology.h's cpu_smt_mask through notify_cpu_starting at the CPUHP_AP_SCHED_STARTING stage into sched_cpu_starting, which is consumed by sched_core_cpu_starting/sched_core_lock for core grouping and multi-rq locking.

I'm flagging that notify_cpu_starting's documented requirement is just that arch code calls it before enabling interrupts on the new cpu, without explicitly guaranteeing the sibling mask is already populated -- so if an architecture sets up sibling cpumasks after this call, cpu_smt_mask could return an empty or incomplete set. This gap sits at the intersection of an existing documented precondition and an unverified ordering assumption, making topology readiness a policy-proposal-level question rather than a confirmed fact. The natural check would be to inspect the target architecture's start_secondary path (e.g., set_cpu_sibling_map) to see whether sibling cpumask setup actually completes before notify_cpu_starting fires.

I'll note I still don't have evidence on exact fill timing across different architectures, or whether cpu_smt_mask gets overridden as a macro somewhere, and treat this as a solid cross-architecture candidate finding to finalize.
